summary: A tight two-player card game where every card can be played several different ways (as a field, a good, a building, or fuel), so most of the tension is in figuring out the most efficient use of a small hand rather than in direct conflict. The real bite is in the scoring: you only count coins from whichever good, beer or bread, you produced less of, so you're constantly forced to keep both economies roughly balanced instead of just maximizing one.
praised: Clever multi-use cards that make each card a small puzzle rather than a single-purpose resource
The lowest-of-two scoring rule creates real tension and forces constant rebalancing instead of a runaway strategy
Fast, satisfying two-player-only design with a lot of depth for its small footprint
Alternating fruitful/dry years give each playthrough a different resource rhythm
criticised: Strictly two players only, so it can't flex to other group sizes
Interaction is mostly indirect (shared field/drafting pressure) rather than confrontational, which can feel low-key for players wanting more conflict
Rules and card text take a session or two to fully click given how much each card can do

interaction.kind: shared drafting pressure and timing squeezes rather than direct conflict

scoring.why: final score is capped by whichever of your two goods (beer or bread) you produced less of, so balancing both tracks decides the winner rather than maximizing either one

similar: Agricola: All Creatures Big and Small
